_Doo kar jod kahe ardhangi, hamku karo tumhari sangi._
_Namdev kahai hamsu mah chhodavo, Ram kaho tumhi gati pavo. ||5||_
_Ab mere tere prit ghatai, brahman mere sada bani aai._
_Rachi chita upar chadhi baitha, tab jiv aay madame paitha. ||6||_
_Brahman sahit jalne jab laga, tab Hari hasat hasat uth bhaga._
_Dhan dhan Namdev sacha bhagta, chhand ekadashi ho raho mugta. ||7||_
_E karam dharam bandha sansara, Ram samar sab chhand pasara._
_Mishrime kyon lon milai, kanjime kyon dudh bhelai. ||8||_
_Bhaktime nahi khot khotai, yame sanshay hai kachhu nahin._
_Duja dharam karo mat koi, bhagat manjh kyon khot hoi._
_Jabte Namdev ekadashi chhandi, tab te Krishn gaye hai sahai. ||9||_

Sakhi.

_...pada sab koy._ ([unclear] -- fragment; the opening half of this line is lost or garbled in the source.)
_Ekadashi maram nahi janahi, bharam bhulaye loy._
_Man to bandhe dvadashi, mugati kahanse loy. ||Vishram||2||_

(4. Then Namdev's mother came; she could not bear the pain of separation from her son.
His wife, folding both hands, said, "Make me your companion." 5. Namdev said, "Give up your attachment to me; chant Ram's name and you too will attain liberation."
"Now the love between you and me has lessened; the Brahmin has become my constant companion." 6. The pyre was built and he sat upon it; then life re-entered the corpse.
When he began to burn along with the Brahmin, the Lord rose up laughing and ran off. 7. "Blessed, blessed is Namdev, the true devotee! Give up Ekadashi and remain free."
"These rites and rituals bind the world; remember Ram and give up all this show." 8. "Why mix salt into sugar-candy? Why mix milk into sour gruel?"
"There is no flaw or falsehood in devotion; there is no doubt at all about this. Let no one practise any other rite; why should there be any flaw amid devotion?" 9. From the time Namdev gave up Ekadashi, from then on Krishna became his helper.

Sakhi: "...all fell." People do not know the secret essence of Ekadashi; they wander lost in delusion. Yet the mind stays bound even on the twelfth day [after breaking the fast] -- from where then would liberation come? Pause -- end of the second sakhi.)

Namdev used to keep the Ekadashi fast. In this way he endured great hardship for two days each fortnight. Then the Lord took the form of a Brahmin and came to him, and on the day of Ekadashi asked him for grain -- but Namdev could not satisfy the Brahmin's request. Namdev said, "O Lord! Do not blame me, do not hold this fault against me. Ask me for whatever milk or curds you need, but on the day of Ekadashi I will not give grain at all. I give none to others, nor do I take any myself. I will not show generosity by giving grain -- if I give grain I would incur sin, and no good would come of it." The Brahmin said, "Listen, O Chhipa! I have wandered through the whole of Jambudwip. I have practised khechari -- the power of flying through the sky (yogamudra) -- that is, I have undertaken the discipline of Ekadashi; but tell me this much: whose salvation has ever come from starving oneself?" (Note -- if you stay hungry, you keep even the Lord hungry too, for the Lord, who accepts the offering from your hand, is kept hungry by you on the day of Ekadashi, and this causes the Lord distress.)

Namdev said, "O Lord! As for why the glory of the practice of Ekadashi has grown, that is proven by the example of Rukmangad, who made all the people of his city -- with true feeling of body and mind -- observe Ekadashi, and thereby brought them all to Vaikunth. I myself know no other secret besides this devotion through Ekadashi. How many devotees like Ambarish, who observed this Ekadashi, should I even count?" The Brahmin then said, "O simple, guileless one, listen -- accept as true what I now tell you. You may keep Ekadashi and the rest, but the essential point is this: just as moonlight can only shine so far, so too, without devotion to the Lord in the form of Ram's name within your heart, such vows remain as dim and pale as moonlight. It is like the buffalo in an oil-presser's house that, while being bathed, eats food mixed with oil residue -- but the day it happens to get food made with ghee instead, and tastes it, the illusion in its mind that oily food was tasty vanishes. In just the same way, these various vow-practices are, in devotion, a wrong method -- like the taste of inferior oil. Without devotion to God, none of these practices can carry one across the ocean of worldly existence. Such vows cannot ferry one across the ocean of birth and death."

Namdev said, "Do not argue and quarrel needlessly; take whatever milk or curds you please, but grain I will not give you." At this, the mocking, jesting Brahmin died right there in his house, as if struck dead. Because of this, a wave of grief and lamentation over the calamity spread through the city. People began to say, "This poor, beggarly so-called devotee is a sinner. What kind of devotion has he attained by killing a Brahmin?" All the suspicious-minded devotees got up and fled from there, saying, "A great sin has attached to you. We do not like this at all. If he were a true devotee of God he would never commit such a sin. Only a sinner would show such a face. Only a sinner would come to meet you now -- for how could the truth of such a sin as yours remain hidden?"

If a person is himself good, the whole world wishes him well; otherwise no one holds any goodwill toward him at all. Yet, in the end, it is only his own soul that can truly judge what is right and wrong -- or rather, only the one upon whom some good or bad effect has actually fallen truly knows the truth of it.

Namdev said, "I too will burn to death together with the Brahmin." Then Namdev fixed his mind wholly upon the Lord. The people of the city came to watch this scene. Large quantities of saffron and sandal-paste were sent for. The Brahmin's body was bathed, a tilak was applied to it, and a silk shroud was sent for to cover it. Namdev's father began to say, "What shall we do now? How shall we live without Namdev?" His father tried to stop him, saying, "Why do you perform such an improper form of devotion? Take the Lord's name in a plain, simple way, sing his praises -- but such a bizarre act should never be done." Then Namdev's mother came; she could not bear the grief of separation from her son. Namdev's wife too, folding both hands, said, "Make me your companion in this as well." Namdev said, "If you now give up your attachment to me and instead sing the name of Ram, you too will attain salvation. Now the love between you and me has lessened; now the situation has arisen that I must join myself to this Brahmin forever." Then, having prepared the pyre, he climbed up and sat upon it -- and at that moment life returned to the Brahmin's corpse. As he began to burn along with the Brahmin, the Lord rose up laughing and delighted, and ran off, saying, "O Namdev! Blessed, blessed are you -- truly you are a genuine devotee! Now give up this Ekadashi and be freed from its bondage. The whole world has become bound up in this kind of ritual observance. So you should only remember and sing the name of Ram, and give up entering into all these other practices. In devotion to Ram's name, which is like the finest sugar, why mix in the salty-and-sweet flavour of rites, chanting, austerities, and vows? Why mix the sour gruel of Ekadashi and other such vows, japa, and austerity, into the pure milk of devotion to Ram's name? In practising devotion to Ram's name, there is no lack, no need whatsoever, for any other kind of devotional practice -- you need have no doubt at all about this. Do not undertake any kind of vow-observance other than devotion to God. There is no deception whatsoever in practising devotion to God." Thus, from the time Lord Krishna gave his help, Namdev gave up observing Ekadashi.

People do not know the secret truth hidden in the matter of Ekadashi. Therefore, caught in the delusion about Ekadashi, people have gone astray in their practice of devotion to God. People, merely imitating others, stay hungry on the day of Ekadashi, but if their mind remains fixed only on when the twelfth day will come so that they can eat, how then can their welfare come about? Because they do not understand the true secret of Ekadashi -- that true Ekadashi means restraining the mind and the senses -- if, instead of grasping this inner meaning, they fix their mind on the objects of the senses, how then can their welfare come about?

Anantdas has stated in this parichari that the entire world is bound up in the ritualistic rites and observances of Ekadashi and other such vows, chanting, and austerities. To demonstrate the glory of Ekadashi, examples such as Rukmangad, Ambarish, and Chandrahas have been given, and efforts have been made to further magnify its glory. Moreover, though people in the present age have become more intelligent, they are still unable to give up the flaw of the practice of Ekadashi, and instead they go on encouraging it. Regarding the example given of Rukmangad, an incident from the present age was found in which a potter and his wife unwittingly attained heaven merely by remaining hungry -- this has been published by Gitapress in Kalyan Masik, Year 65, Issue 4, page 521, and has also been printed a third time in later compilations. In Year 55, Issue 10, page 839, the following is written:

Once, India's renowned, late (departed into the eternal Brahman), venerable Shankaracharya of the Jyotishpith, revered and glorious Krishnabodhashramji Maharaj, came to Vishwanathpuri-Kashi. That day was Ekadashi. In keeping with his own rule, the revered Acharyaji himself observed the fast of complete abstention from food on Ekadashi, and was also urging other people to keep the Ekadashi fast. Along with telling everyone to keep the Ekadashi fast, he would also tell them that just as eating grain on the day of Ekadashi is a sin, so too drinking tea, and consuming tobacco, bidis, and other such intoxicating substances, and chewing paan, on the day of Ekadashi, is even more sinful. What kind of Ekadashi fast is it in which tea, tobacco, and such things are consumed? Drinking tea, tobacco, ganja, and the like produces a tamasic (dull, base) disposition, and causes auspicious undertakings to come to nought. Therefore one should always abstain from these harmful habits. In this dreadful age of Kali, keeping the Ekadashi fast, chanting the names of the Lord -- Shri Ram, or Krishna, or Shri Shiv -- daily offering water to the sun, bathing in the holy Ganga, listening to sacred recitations (katha), and living a simple, virtuous life according to one's own varna and ashrama dharma, and remaining devoted daily to the service of cows -- these are the direct means to the welfare of the soul.

One day the revered Acharya asked a young Brahmin celibate (brahmachari) who had come to him, "Brahmachari! Have you kept the Ekadashi fast today?"

The brahmachari replied, "No, Maharajji."

The revered Jagadguru said, "Being a Hindu, and moreover born into a Brahmin family, and being a brahmachari besides -- and still you have not kept the Ekadashi fast? This is indeed a matter of great surprise."

The brahmachari said, "Maharajji! I never keep the Ekadashi fast at all."

The revered Jagadguru said, "Ah! Then how are you a Hindu at all? How are you fit to be called a brahmachari, and how are you a Brahmin, if you cannot even keep the Ekadashi fast?

Keeping the Ekadashi fast has a truly wondrous and extraordinary glory, which is mentioned in all our scriptures and Puranas. Keeping the Ekadashi fast carries very great glory and immense merit, which people today, out of foolishness, have forgotten. One who keeps the Ekadashi fast has no fear whatsoever, in the next world, of being beaten or tormented by Yama's messengers. Through it our welfare comes about in every way. This is stated in our scriptures and Puranas. This is not mere idle talk or imagination -- it is absolutely true, word for word.

We once met two Muslims who, though of a different faith, used to observe the fast on every Ekadashi."

Hearing this much from the revered Acharya's own mouth, the people present grew curious and eager to hear the full account concerning the Muslim brothers who kept the Ekadashi fast, and they requested the revered Acharya for it. Then the revered Maharaj related the true incident from beginning to end, as follows.

The Acharyaji said, "Once, while we were touring to spread the Sanatan Dharma, we had gone to Rajasthan. There we were given lodging in a garden, and that day happened to be the sacred day of Ekadashi. Many devoted followers had come to see us there. Among them, two Muslim gentlemen also came to meet us. They greeted us from a distance and sat down to one side. When one of our brahmacharis began distributing, as prasad, some fruits that had been brought as offerings, to everyone present, I told that brahmachari, 'Brother, give some prasad to those Muslim brothers sitting there too!' Accordingly, when the brahmachari came forward to give prasad to the two Muslims, both of them, with great reverence and devotion, folded their hands and said humbly, 'Maharajji! Today happens to be our day of Ekadashi. Both of us keep a waterless fast on the day of Ekadashi. So today we shall not accept anything at all.'

"Hearing from the mouths of these Muslim brothers that they kept a waterless fast on the day of Ekadashi, everyone was greatly astonished, and along with that grew eager to know the whole matter -- what possible connection or purpose Muslim brothers could have with keeping the Ekadashi vow. Out of curiosity, I called the two gentlemen near and asked them, 'You are both Muslims. Then, being Muslim, what is the reason and purpose behind your keeping the waterless Ekadashi fast? Only Hindus, after all, keep the waterless Ekadashi fast. Since when, and how, did you people begin keeping the Ekadashi fast? Tell us the whole matter.'

"In reply, the two Muslim brothers, recounting a great and astonishing true incident from their own lives, told us how, by our unwittingly keeping a false fast on the day of Ekadashi, we were saved from the torment of Yama in the next world. They related: 'Although both of us are Muslim by caste, we make our living by driving a cart and carrying goods and loads from one place to another. One day we had taken our cart out for hire. We were so occupied that day with the work of driving the cart that we got nothing at all to eat or drink the whole day. In this way both of us remained completely hungry and thirsty that day, and we went and stopped in a garden. Being hungry, thirsty, and tired, we fell asleep. That day, three other people were also lodging in that same garden, and they were cooking and eating food. That night we saw that we had died. Fearsome-looking messengers of Yama came to us and seized all five of us men. They took us to Yamapuri. There we saw a person seated on a beautiful throne -- an extremely radiant royal figure, like the sun. He asked his attendant-messengers who had seized and brought us, \'Why have you brought these two here, having seized them? These two have kept the waterless fast of Ekadashi today. Take them away from here at once. Take them back to the very place from which you seized them, and leave them there. Because of the merit of the Ekadashi fast, some days have been added to their allotted life-span.\'

"'On his order, the Yamdoots brought us both back and left us again in that same garden. When we returned into our own bodies and regained consciousness, we opened our eyes, and the two of us began talking to each other about what had happened in the other world. Every detail became directly known to us. We were greatly astonished. Of the whole experience, what we especially remembered was the matter of keeping the waterless Ekadashi fast. We had, in passing, occasionally heard something of this from the mouths of our Hindu brothers, but had never paid it any special attention. Before this, in our whole lives up to that point, we had never once thought of keeping the Ekadashi fast, nor did we know anything about it. We were greatly astonished that, being Muslims who did not even know how to keep the Ekadashi fast, we had nonetheless been declared and accepted there as observers of the Ekadashi fast. To find out the full truth, we came straight back to our village and first sought out a Hindu pandit. Going to him, we asked, \'Panditji! What was yesterday's date among the Hindus, and what vow was it?\' In reply the pandit told us that it had been the meritorious fast-day of Bhimseni Ekadashi. Now, learning this from the pandit, our astonishment knew no bounds. We told the pandit the whole matter, and hearing it, the pandit said that such a thing was indeed possible, and with great affection explained to us the glory of Ekadashi and some other matters of Hindu scripture as well. Learning and hearing of such a wondrous glory of the Hindus' Ekadashi fast, from that very day a great faith in the Ekadashi fast arose within us. Thus, without any resolve or intention, merely by unknowingly remaining hungry and thirsty on the day of Ekadashi, we obtained the fruit of keeping the Ekadashi fast; and even without keeping the Ekadashi fast, we were accepted as observers of it -- and as a result, that false Ekadashi fast of ours saved us from the torment of Yama and from death. So then, if we were to keep it in earnest, every single Ekadashi, what limit could there be to our great merit?' Thinking thus, from that time on, both of us have regularly kept the fast on every Ekadashi day.

"'On the day of Ekadashi we take neither food nor water at all. Though we are Muslims, we keep the Ekadashi fast, and from that very day we have also given up forever eating meat, fish, eggs, chicken, and other such violence-tainted forbidden foods. Now we have come to believe that one should live only a simple life that is sattvic, righteous, pure, and religious.'" Hearing this account of the glory of the Ekadashi fast from the mouths of those Muslim brothers, everyone was greatly astonished.

Thus the above episode concerning the Muslims is meant to demonstrate the glory of Ekadashi. Had Yamaraj, instead of sending these two brothers back to the mortal world, granted them liberation on account of the merit of Ekadashi and sent them straight to heaven, we would not even have had this account of Ekadashi's glory. Other forms of worship too display such wonders as this. But such acts of worship do not bring about our true liberation. Shri Jivanji Maharaj calls such wonders "zabak-jhooth" -- a flash of falsehood -- meaning something that appears real only for a fleeting moment, but which in truth holds no reality.

In presenting Kabirji's sakhi in the Samagam, it is said:

_Kabir ekadashi ludi karun, tirath karun gulam._
_Ek Ramahi ram raha, tasu karu salam. ||1||_
_Kot kot ekadashi, maha prasadko ansh._
_Vyas jako man paratit hai, jaka guru Harivansh. ||2||_

(Kabir says: I shall make Ekadashi my lowly maidservant, and turn pilgrimage into my slave; but to the one who abides absorbed only in the one Ram, to him alone shall I bow in salutation. Crores upon crores of Ekadashis are but a fraction of the great prasad of devotion; such is the faith in Vyas's mind -- he whose guru is Harivansh.)

In the devotee-poet Vyasji collection, on page 420, in the fifth citation, the above sakhi appears as follows:

_Koti koti ekadashi, mahaprasang kau ans._
_Vyas hi yah paratiti hai, jinke guru Haribans. ||2||_

(Crores upon crores of Ekadashis are but a fraction of the great occasion of devotion; this itself is Vyas's faith -- he whose guru is Haribans.)

Das Kabirji says that he will reduce Ekadashi to the status of a lowly, worthless maidservant of his, and will disregard it; and he will make pilgrimage his slave -- that is, treat it like his servant. But whoever is a devotee in whose heart devotion to Ram has pervaded, him alone will he honour and receive with respect.

Vyasdasji says that crores upon crores of Ekadashis do not count for anything at all in comparison with the Lord's prasad -- that is, they are trivial before the great prasad. Hence it is Vyas's firm conviction that the great prasad of devotion is far superior to Ekadashi. Such is Vyasji, whose beloved guru, Harivanshji, says this.

Hence, the true Ekadashi of the Vaishnavs:

_Ek mana ekadashi, Harko vrat dhariye._
_Namdev nam jahaj hai, bhavsagar tariye._

(Ekadashi with a one-pointed mind -- that is the true vow of the Lord to keep; Namdev says the Name is a ship by which we cross the ocean of worldly existence.)

Namdev says that for Vaishnavs, true Ekadashi means this: devotion to the Lord practised with a one-pointed mind and single-minded devotion is what should be reckoned as such -- for the Lord's Name is like a grand, great ship, by which we can cross over the ocean of worldly existence.

The above words are from a Velaval composed by Namdev. That Velaval is as follows:

(Source: Panchratnamala, Chapter 4, page 575)

|| Velaval ||

_Bhai re -- tattva kahanku Ram hai, bhaji lijo soi._
_Lila sindhu agadh hai, gat lakhe jan koi. ||Tek||_
_Jog jagnathe kaha sare, tirath asnana,_
_Ose pyas na bhaj hi, bhajiye Bhagavana. ||Tattva||1||_
_Kanchan Meru saman hai, gaj dijo dana,_
_Kot gau jo dan de, nahi nam samana. ||Tattva||2||_
_Pujanku sadhu jana, Harike adhikari,_
_Unse Govind paiye, eh paropakari. ||Tattva||3||_
_Ek mana ekadashi, Hariko vrat dhariye,_
_Namdev nam jahaj hai, bhavsagar tariye. ||Tattva||4||_

(O brother -- the essential truth is that it is Ram, so worship him alone. His playful ocean is unfathomable; scarcely any soul can fathom its depth. Refrain.
1. What use are yoga, sacrificial rites, or bathing at pilgrimage places? They do not quench the thirst -- worship God instead.
2. Even if one donates gold as much as Mount Meru, or gives an elephant in charity, or gives away crores of cows in charity, nothing equals the Lord's Name.
3. For worship, holy men are the rightful recipients of the Lord's grace; through serving them we attain Govind -- that is the truly beneficial course.
4. Ekadashi kept with a single-pointed mind -- that is the true vow of the Lord; Namdev says the Name is a ship, by which we cross the ocean of worldly existence.)

Namdev says: O devotee brothers! If you wish to know what the true, original nature of God actually is, then sing only the name of Ram. The playful sports of the Lord, who is like an ocean of divine play (lila), are boundless; only some rare saint or devotee can grasp the deep meaning of his lila. As for the practice of yogic disciplines by yogis, or the performance of sacrifices and such rites -- none of these can make attainment of the divine reality possible; nor does undertaking pilgrimage bring any benefit at all. Just as thirst cannot be quenched by dew-drops, so too nothing can be accomplished by such yoga, sacrifice, or bathing at pilgrimage sites. Therefore, to attain God, one must sing his praises -- even if one were to give in charity gold in quantity equal to Mount Meru, or donate vast animals like elephants, or give away crores of cows, none of this could equal the Lord's Name. Therefore, if one wishes to render service and worship, the truly beneficial course is to serve and keep the company of saints, who are worthy recipients of the Lord's grace; it is only through serving them that we can attain God -- such saints, who bring this about, are truly beneficent. Namdev says: for Vaishnavs, true Ekadashi is to be understood as this -- devotion practised toward the Lord with a one-pointed mind and single-minded faith -- for the Lord's Name is like a grand, great ship, by which we can cross over the ocean of worldly existence.

Jivandasji says:

_Abhe vrat ekadashi, nit nit Ganga nahay._
_Sitapati bin Jivana, kal kaleja mahe. ||160||_

(Whoever keeps the vow of Ekadashi, and daily bathes in the Ganga -- without Sitapati [Ram, husband of Sita], says Jivan, death still lodges within his very heart.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: even if one believes that keeping the Ekadashi fast removes the fear of Yamaraj's torment, and, believing that bathing daily in the Ganga removes the fear of Yamaraj, keeps the Ekadashi vow and bathes daily in the Ganga -- still, without devotion to the name of Ram, the fear of death continues to dwell within your own heart.

To magnify the glory of Ekadashi, examples of Rukmangad, Ambarish, Chandrahas, and -- wrongly -- even Namdevji, are cited; and in the same way, another illustrative story is also given. This story is given in Sandipini, Part 2, page 3, Registration No. 221, as follows:

An illustrative story on why one should not eat grain on Ekadashi.

_Ekadashyam tu papam hi chaannam aashritya tishthati,_
_tasmaj janair na bhoktavyam drashtanto'tra na bhojane._

(On Ekadashi, sin itself takes up residence within grain; therefore people should not eat it -- here is the illustrative story regarding this non-eating.)

On the day of Ekadashi, sin comes and dwells within grain; for this reason people should not eat grain that day. Why should one not eat it? What is the reason? Here is the illustrative story on this. Dharma was born from Shri Vishnuji, and from Dharma all righteous beings came to be. Then Dharmaraj found he had no work left to do, so he went and complained to Vishnuji that he had no task. Vishnuji thought deeply over this. As he sat pondering, a drop of sweat fell from his back, and from it Adharma was born. Vishnuji sent Adharma down to the mortal world, and because of it many human beings became sinners. Now Yamaraj, being kept so busy dealing with sinners, found he had no leisure even to eat, so he too complained that he had no free time. Vishnuji then removed Adharma from the mortal world. Adharma went to Vishnulok, and Vishnuji said, "Here in Vaikunth there is no place for you -- go to Brahma." He went to Brahmalok. Brahmaji too turned him away, saying, "Here only sacred discourse takes place; there is no place for you here." Then he went to Kailash, and Shivji ran at him with a trident to strike him. Then he came back again to Vishnuji and said, "I was born from you -- now where shall I go?" Then Vishnuji, after reflection, said, "You shall dwell in the mortal world every other day, and on the day of Ekadashi you shall reside within grain." This is why one should not eat grain on Ekadashi.

Kabirji has said -- from Kabirvani, Issue 127, front page:

_Rakhe varat ekadashi, kare annako tyag._
_Bhang tamakhu na tajai, kahain Kabir abhag._

(He keeps the Ekadashi fast, giving up grain -- yet does not give up bhang and tobacco; such a person, says Kabir, is unfortunate.)

People keep the Ekadashi vow and give up grain on that day, but they do not give up bhang, tobacco, and other intoxicating substances. Swami Kabir says that such people are unfortunate -- they do not give up the intoxicating substances that prevent the vow from being fulfilled and render it fruitless. How, then, can the fruit of the vow be obtained? If one wishes to make one's means of spiritual welfare succeed, one must give up intoxication.

Parashuram says:

_Ekadashi eki dasha, bujhe virla sant._
_Parsa mare mathari, nathi jani shank._

(Ekadashi is a single, inner state -- only a rare saint understands it; others merely dish out and eat fried snacks, with no thought spared for its true meaning.)

Parashuram says: Ekadashi, in its true sense, means keeping one's inclinations single-pointedly fixed in the state of devotion to God alone -- but this secret is understood only by some rare people. All the rest simply gorge themselves on sweet dishes such as dudhpak. Because of this, all their observances lack true sincerity and appear doubtful, and so their observances turn out fruitless and go to waste.

We may observe that Karmabai fed Lord Jagannathji khichdi out of loving devotion. Not knowing the rules of ritual purity, in her simple innocence, without bathing or purifying herself or preparing a ritually clean cooking-space, she used to offer khichdi as prasad to the Lord, and the Lord would eat that prasad lovingly. Even today, at Jagannathji's temple, khichdi is offered as prasad in Karmabai's name. In the province of Orissa, at Jagannathji's temple, the practice of Ekadashi does not exist; hence at Jagannathji, Ekadashi is said to be "hung upside down." Moreover, in Orissa, among those who observe the Ekadashi vow there, the custom is that even while having kept the Ekadashi fast, one may eat rice at that time. Thus, in this place, people eat rice on Ekadashi. Those who fast eat fruit and fill their stomachs, yet still count it as a fast. Indeed, on the day of Ekadashi such people eat double the usual amount, taking delight in eating tasty fruit-based food. In this way they turn Ekadashi itself into a mere "Ekadashi in name." In its true sense, the spirit of Ekadashi is meant to be observed by mastering, subduing, the eleven senses -- for "gyaras" (eleven) is meant to be conquered.

1. Charandasi sect, 2. Harishchandri, 3. a branch of the Gopalia sect, 4. Santram, 5. the Radhavallabh sect -- this is a branch of the Radhavallabhi sect. This appears to be understood as a branch of the Nimbarka sect. On the day of Ekadashi, their acharya was once given a paan-bidi and ate it; because of this, that sect rejected Ekadashi outright, and it is said that this tradition of not observing Ekadashi arose from that incident. Even today, it is said, these people do not observe Ekadashi. (Registration No. 541, page 297.)

The publishers of Moksha Patrika, who had gone to Jagannath, felt sorrow that Ekadashi is not observed there; this is written in that periodical, Registration No. 240, page 201.

"The Ekadashi shrine -- the shrine of Ekadashi is located behind the main temple. Here, at Jagannathji, Ekadashi is said to be hung upside down. Hence no one here keeps the Ekadashi fast. In the whole scheme of the prasad, the practice of fasting on that day appears to have stopped entirely here. We did not like this. Therefore we ourselves kept the Ekadashi fast here."

Sadguru Kabirji, in a Ramaini, has made a fine, pointed remark about Ekadashi.

|| Ramaini ||

_Manki khod kar mere bhai, atam china bina mukti nahi pai._
_Hindu musalman dono bade kasbi, eke lini mala duje lini tasbi._
_Hindu musalman dono pad gai aanti, ek jalave dujo dale mati._
_Ek puje dera duja puje dhora, jaki bhatiyan le gaye kala chora._
_Ek rahewe ekadashi duja rahewe roza, jaka tan man haji nahi khoja._
_Ek puje sura ek puje asura, guruke bhajan bina donu mat adhura._
_Kahe Kabir sun man ledu, e bolan har musalman ke hindu._

(O my mind, my brother, search deeply within -- without recognizing the true self, liberation cannot be attained. Hindus and Muslims are both great masters of outward craft -- one took up the mala, the other the tasbih. Hindu and Muslim, both fell into a tangled knot of dispute -- one burns the dead, the other buries them. One worships at the temple, the other worships at the tomb; their intelligence has been stolen away, corrupted like thieves in the dark. One keeps Ekadashi, the other keeps Roza -- yet neither has truly examined his own body and mind. One worships the gods, the other worships the demonic; without devotion through the Guru's teaching, both remain incomplete. Kabir says: listen, O mind -- is the very principle that inspires you from within a Hindu, or is it a Muslim?)

O my mind, my brother! Reflect a little more deeply. Without understanding one's own true self, liberation cannot be attained. Both Hindus and Muslims are, as it were, great masters of outward craft and skill; between these two -- Hindu and Muslim -- enmity and discord have arisen out of mere confusion. One burns the corpse, the other buries it. One worships in a temple, the other worships at a tomb. Because of this, the intelligence of both has become thoroughly corrupted, deceitful, and thief-like. One observes the Ekadashi fast, the other keeps the roza and remains hungry -- yet neither of their minds is truly fixed in genuine contemplation. Thus, among them, one worships the gods and another engages in demonic forms of worship; but without devotion, in accordance with the true Guru's teaching, the practices of both remain incomplete. Kabirji says: O mind! Listen to the true secret -- is the very principle that inspires you from within a Hindu, or is it a Muslim?

After discussing Ekadashi, the Samagam gives a special instruction concerning the Ganga: regarding this, the Vaishnav Jivandasji himself said, "In devotion to Vishnu, if such a thief posing as an honest merchant keeps circling ahead of one, again and again, the soul does not attain liberation. The origin of the Ganga -- its beginning, end, and middle extent -- that too is [explained through] that thief."

Regarding this, the Vaishnav Jivandasji said that in this way, in the practice of devotion to Vishnu, if such a "merchant-thief" keeps circling ahead again and again, the soul cannot attain liberation. He then spoke further of the question of the Ganga -- he would explain, at length, the origin of the Ganga: its beginning, end, and middle.

Long ago, the Sanakadik sages -- Sanak, Sanatan, Sanandan, and Sanatkumar -- were the four sons born of Brahma's maya. All four, being of one nature, sat down together to perform austerities. They performed intense, fierce austerity. They kept Brahma's water-pot (kamandal) set between them as they sat. Drops of sweat fell from the foreheads of the four onto the kamandal, and as it filled up, it came to be called the "Brahma-kamandal." Taking with them this wealth -- the treasure of their yogic power and glory -- they went before Brahma. Brahma was delighted and granted his sons a boon: "May you remain forever, always, as children; may desire never arise in you; may you never be separated from sight of me." He gave this boon to all four. Then Brahma thought: this is the wealth of their austerity, in the form of the water of their sweat within this kamandal; it would be good if its glory increased. So Brahma told Narada to spread the glory of the Sanakadiks' austerity-wealth throughout the three worlds.

Hearing this word, Narada came down to the mortal world. King Sagar's sixty thousand sons had been burnt to ashes by Kapilji, and they had not attained liberation. For this reason, Narada came to Ayodhya. In the third generation after King Sagar of the Solar dynasty was King Bhagirath. Narada told him that if the Ganga were to come to the mortal world, his ancestors would be delivered. Then King Bhagirath sat down to perform austerities. Then Naradaji spoke to the Gracious Lord, saying that King Bhagirath was suffering greatly. Then the Gracious Lord said, "Long ago, when I deceived King Bali, I placed and measured three strides across the three worlds. I placed one foot at King Bali's door; I placed the second foot in the mortal world, at the city of Puratpattan; I placed the third foot in Brahmalok." At that time, a thought arose in Brahma's mind: "There is Ganga water in my kamandal -- let me use that water to wash Vasudev's feet, and take the resulting charanamrit." And in Rudra's mind arose the thought: "If we can obtain Hari's charanamrit and place it on our head, my poison would be cured." The Lord knew this, but Brahma's wish remained only in his mind. As the Lord placed his third step, the blow of his right big toe caused the kamandal to tip over and spill, and so Brahma's wish did not reach fulfilment.

Here a question arises: at the feet of the Gracious Lord dwell his saints and devotees; and the water in that kamandal, being the sweat of the Sanakadik sages, is itself a leftover, impure substance -- so how could it be offered at the feet of Vasudev? Regarding this, there is a saying from Madho Gosai's meditative-lila composition:

_Je pad param prakshalate Bal dhare do hath,_
_te pad ud kataksh bhedi aani hai Gang._

(Those feet which King Bali held with both hands to wash and receive as the supreme purification -- from those very feet, pierced open by his loving glance, the Ganga was drawn forth, soaring upward.)

Madho Gosai says: those very feet of Lord Vamana, which King Bali held out with both hands in order to wash them and receive their nectar -- it is through that same Vamana's cosmic universal form breaking through the concave inner surface of the universe that the Ganga was brought down and made to descend.

Here follows a verse from Jayadevji's Ashtapadi:

_Chhalayasi vikramane balim adbhuta-Vamana,_
_padanakha-nira-janita-jana-pavana._
_Keshava dhrita-Vamana-rupa jaya jagadisha Hare. ||75||_

(O wondrous Vamana! By your strides you deceived Bali; from the water sprung from your toenail you purify the people. O Keshav, who assumed the form of Vamana, victory to you! O Hari, O Lord of the universe, victory to you!)

O wondrous Vamana! You deceived Bali while measuring out your strides, by the water that came forth from your toenail, through which you have purified the people. O Keshav, who has assumed the form of Vamana, victory to you! O Hari, O Lord of the universe, victory to you!

Here follows a verse on the glory of the Gangashtakam:

_Bhagavati bhavalila-mauli-male tavambhah kanam anuparimanam praninoye sprishanti,_
_amara-nagara-nari chamara-grahininam vihata-kali-kalankatankam anke lunthanti. ||76||_

(O Divine Mother, garland upon the crown of Shiva's cosmic play -- those beings who touch even an atom-sized drop of your water become freed from the terror of Kali Yuga's stain, and come to roll in the laps of the celestial city's women who hold chamaras in their hands.) -- Shankaracharya, Gangashtak, verse 3.

Like a garland upon the crest of Shankar's divine play, O goddess Ganga! Those people who touch even an atom-sized drop of your water become freed of the terrifying stain of the Kali Yuga, and go to sport in the laps of the women who dwell in the city of the gods, holding chamaras in their hands.

_Brahmanda khandayanti Hari-shirasi jata-vallim ullasayanti,_
_svarlokad apatanti kanakagiri-guha-gandashailat skhalanti,_
_kshoni-prishthe lunthanti durita-chaya-chamoor nirbharam bhartsayanti,_
_pathodhim purayanti sura-nagara-sarit pavani nah punatu. ||77||_

(Breaking through the universe, making the creeper of matted locks on Hari-Shiva's head shine, falling down from the heavenly realm, tumbling from the rocky slopes of the golden mountain's caves, rolling upon the surface of the earth, sternly rebuking the vast army-like mass of sins, filling the ocean -- may that pure river of the celestial city purify us.)

Breaking through the universe, making the creeper of matted locks upon the head of Lord Shankar shine, falling down from heaven, tumbling from the mountain slopes and cave-mouths of the golden mountain, rolling upon the surface of the earth, sternly rebuking the massed army of sins, filling the ocean -- may such a pure Ganga river purify us.

For this reason Mahadevji, knowing that it would cool his throat, held the Ganga in his matted locks. Brahma remained struck with astonishment (for, going to wash the Lord's feet, his kamandal had been knocked over by the Lord's toe, and so he had not been able to wash the feet). Therefore the Lord told Naradji to go and ask Rudra to fulfil Bhagirath's wish. Then Naradji came to Rudra and related Bhagirath's story at length. Thereupon Mahadevji released a lock of his matted hair. From it a stream burst forth, extending sixty thousand yojanas. From this, two streams formed. One stream rushed down into Patal; going to King Bali's abode, it touched the feet of Vasudev there, and thereby became purified. The second stream flowed on ahead of King Bhagirath. Bowing in reverence, he led the Ganga on into the mortal world.

Bhagirath did not know that the great sage Jahnu was seated in austerity on Mount Himachal. Jahnu let Bhagirath go on ahead, and then, gathering the Ganga in his cupped hands, drank her up entirely. Afterward, when Bhagirath looked back, he could not see the Ganga anywhere. He then realized this was the power of sage Jahnu's great austerity, and so praised the sage in a hymn. The sage, delighted and pleased, then split open his right thigh and released the Ganga from it. Because sage Jahnu thus drank her and released her, the sage Shantanu gave her the name "Jahnavi Ganga." And because Bhagirath brought her, she was named "Bhagirathi Ganga."

As for the name "Ganga" itself: "gagan" means the forehead of the head -- for nothing is found as elevated as it, and the microcosm of the body corresponds to the macrocosm of the universe. Since the water arose from the sweat of the foreheads of the Sanakadik sages, and the forehead is like a "sky" (gagan), and that water belongs to Brahmalok, which is likewise in the sky -- therefore "ga" stands for "gagan" (sky), and within it "ga" also means "one who moves, one who flows" -- for this reason she was named "Ganga." Because she issued from Shankar's matted locks, she was named "Shankari." Because she touched Vasudev's feet through the kamandal, she was named "Vishnupadodaki," she who springs from Vishnu's feet. When five thousand years of the Kali Yuga have passed, the sixty thousand sons of King Sagar will attain liberation; at that time King Bhagirath will give the command, and from there the Ganga will come to rest upon Mahadevji's head -- she will go to where he holds her in his matted locks.

Sakhi.

_Hari charanse upani, padi Shiv shir dhar._
_Mrityu loke aavi Jivana, bhulya sab sansar. ||1||_

(Springing forth from Hari's feet, she fell as a stream upon Shiva's head; thus, says Jivan, she came into the mortal world -- yet the whole world has gone astray about her true meaning.)
